headline: Flight chaos, a Microsoft outage and a fight over Brampton's auto plant
summary: Two technology failures hit daily life: a Microsoft outage that cut email at Toronto hospitals and a U.S. air traffic breakdown that cancelled thousands of flights. Ottawa moved against Stellantis over the sale of its Brampton plant while Carney tied any U.S. trade deal to autos. Abroad, the Strait of Hormuz stayed largely shut, and late U.S. election calls widened Democrats' gains.

top.headline: Hormuz stays mined and blockaded as Trump weighs holding off on new strikes
top.what: Iran reported more tankers striking mines in the Strait of Hormuz, traffic stayed about 65% below pre-war levels and the U.S. kept its blockade of Iranian ports. Brent crude still fell about 2.5% on the week to near US$96 a barrel, and Trump was reported to be leaning against new attacks unless provoked.
top.why: The strait's closure is the main force behind high fuel prices and the inflation that has central banks raising rates.

top.headline: Nationwide FAA ground stop cancels thousands of flights, including Toronto's U.S. routes
top.what: A network failure halted all U.S. departures for more than four hours on Friday, the longest such stop since 2001; more than 5,000 further flights were cancelled Saturday and Air Canada said about 27,000 of its passengers were affected. Officials blame a router installed during a contractor's fibre upgrade.
top.why: It stranded GTA travellers on cross-border routes and exposed how fragile U.S. air traffic control equipment is.

top.headline: Ottawa starts 30-day default clock on Stellantis over Brampton plant sale
top.what: After Stellantis agreed to sell its idled Brampton assembly plant to armoured-vehicle maker Roshel, Ottawa served a notice of default on its subsidy agreement and, with Ontario, offered a package to stop the sale. Carney said Saturday the government is not satisfied with the company.
top.why: Thousands of laid-off Brampton auto workers and up to $529 million in public commitments are at stake.

top.headline: Carney says U.S. trade deal is closer but autos are a red line
top.what: The prime minister said in Manila that a two-country deal is possible but not yet done, and that Canada will not sign one that leaves its auto sector unviable. U.S. Democrats, who take over Congress in January, say they will try to repeal tariffs on Canada but cannot override a veto.
top.why: Tariffs on autos and steel are the biggest threat to Ontario manufacturing jobs, with new vehicle tariffs threatened for January.

top.headline: Late calls extend Democratic gains; Alaska Senate race still open
top.what: Democrats added the Kansas and Alaska governorships and Mississippi's Senate seat as counting finished, bringing them to 30 governors. In Alaska's Senate race, Mary Peltola leads Sen. Dan Sullivan by more than 10,000 votes but sits just under 50%, with a ranked-choice count set for Nov. 18.
top.why: A larger Democratic majority in Congress from January shapes U.S. policy on tariffs, spending and oversight of the Trump administration.

top.headline: Nvidia scandal topples Huang and puts Commerce Secretary Lutnick under pressure
top.what: Nvidia's shares sank and Jensen Huang stepped down as chief executive over chip sales to Megaspeed International, and the fallout reached cabinet as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pointed at the Commerce Department. Trump advisers have discussed Howard Lutnick's future, though the president still backs him.
top.why: Nvidia is one of the most widely held stocks in Canadian retirement and index funds, and the affair touches U.S. export controls on China.

top.headline: Microsoft outage knocks out email at Toronto hospitals, schools and governments
top.what: A worldwide failure of Outlook, Teams and other Microsoft services began Thursday, prompting a Code Grey at Unity Health Toronto and disrupting universities, city hall, federal departments and VIA Rail. Microsoft declared everything restored early Saturday and blamed a network upgrade.
top.why: It showed how much hospitals and public services rely on a single company's online systems.

top.headline: Ukraine talks end without a land deal; Zelenskyy says U.S. floated Donbas-for-NATO swap
top.what: U.S.-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi produced a prisoner exchange of more than 1,000 people but no agreement on territory. Zelenskyy said American envoys raised trading parts of the Donbas for NATO membership, and EU leaders named a five-country team to represent Europe.
top.why: Any settlement would reshape European security and Canada's NATO and aid commitments.
